Now when the Greeks heard that Diogenes had been captured,
they proclaimed as their king Michael, the son of Constantine.
And he seized his mother,
her who had been the wife of Diogenes,
and by force made her dwell in a monastery.
And his uncle John became Caesar to him.
Now Diogenes, when he entered the land of the Romans
and heard what had happened,
went up to the fortress of Doukeia,
and found in it two hundred thousand dinars,
and sent them to the Sultan with those two emirs who had gone with him,
and informed him of the matter.
And he put on the monastic habit
and took up residence in Doukeia.
And he sent to Michael and said:
"I, up to now, have fought the good fight on behalf of the confession of the Christians,
and it is enough for me.
As for you, blessed is your kingdom,
and you have done well to take the throne,
because it was rightfully yours.
However, in all faithfulness I advise you not to break the peace which I made with the Sultan;
otherwise, no peace will remain,
neither for you,
nor for the Christians {OCR?}."
And Michael accepted his kindness and said:
"I will not depart from your counsel."
A few days later, however, certain men incited him,
and he sent to Diogenes and said to him:
"If in truth you are a monk,
why should you dwell in a fortress? It is proper that you should go down to one of the monasteries,
so that we may send guards into it, into the fortress."
Then Diogenes was enraged and said:
"Out of the whole empire of the Romans he does not even leave me one fortress!"
And he arose, stripped off his woolen garments,
and took the merchandise of the merchants of Doukeia by way of a loan,
and gathered an army for himself.
And when the son of Sennacherib, the patrician of Lesser Armenia, came to him,
he seized him and gouged out his eyes,
and took from him eighty quintals of gold.
And he became very powerful and came to Melitene,
and sent to Sultan Alp Arslan
and asked for help from him.
And the Sultan promised him
that he himself would go in person to help him wherever the occasion called.
And after these things,
Diogenes departed from Melitene to Cilicia {OCR?}.
And John came against him
and besieged him in the city of Adana.
And when he had seized him,
he sent word to King Michael.
